clue.text: What's not real? Defending habit, I'm saying it is

indicators.note: to defend is to surround and protect, so one piece wraps round the other here

parts.note: a myth is a story that is not real
a rut is a fixed habit or routine

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about fantasy, answered by someone insisting their stubborn habit is real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defending' wraps one piece round the other. The definition is a whole phrase: the modern 'my truth' is what I say is true for me.
explanation.definitionFit: The modern idiom 'my truth' means a personal account that the speaker insists is true for them.

clue.text: Working method required to cover large part of course

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

indicators.note: to cover means to sit over and enclose something, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: due means owed or required

explanation.surface: A method of study needed to get through a large part of a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' sends the large abbreviation inside the word for required. 'Working method' is modus operandi, abbreviated MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A module is a self-contained unit of study, so it forms one part of a course.

clue.text: Flourish of trumpets at the start — king entering queen's home

indicators.note: at the start says take only the opening letter of the word
entering means going into, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a queen bee lives in a hive
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A fanfare of trumpets announces a king entering the queen's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' gives T from trumpets; 'entering' puts R (rex) into HIVE, the queen bee's home. 'Flourish of trumpets' reads as a fanfare.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive is to grow vigorously and prosper, a synonym of the verb flourish.

clue.text: Item turned up unbroken

indicators.note: up here means stirred up or disturbed, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something turned up in perfect condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like the signal, but it is part of the material: 'up' rearranges ITEM TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unremitted means never let up or relaxed, so continuous and without a break.

clue.text: Nothing gained by rustic cricket shot (not one for purists)

indicators.note: gained by means taken in by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hick is an unsophisticated country person
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin's crude cricket shot earns him nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gained by' puts O inside HICK. In cricket a hoick is an ugly, cross-batted swipe of the ball to leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoick is a crude heaving stroke, frowned on by cricket's purists who prefer classical technique.

clue.text: Comic patter not right — starts to make tasteless crack

indicators.note: comic suggests something played about for laughs, so the letters are jumbled
not tells us a letter is to be left out of patter
starts to says take only the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A comedian's patter falls flat, sliding into tasteless wisecracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' removes R from PATTER, leaving PATTE; 'starts to' supplies M and T from 'make tasteless'; 'Comic' rearranges PATTEMT.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a crack at something is to make an attempt at it, so the noun senses match.

clue.text: 8! That's early in the morning for some into raves

parts.words: That's early in the morning for some
parts.note: at ten o'clock is an early start for some people

indicators.note: to rave is to talk wildly, so the letters of the word run wild

explanation.surface: Ravers think ten in the morning is early.
explanation.walkthrough: AT TEN is early for a late riser; 'raves' rearranges INTO. 8 is TAKE NOTE, which, with '!', means the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are commands to heed something: 'Attention!' and 'Take note!' call for notice.

clue.text: Next time — what about November?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: eh is an exclamation asking 'what?'
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the next occasion: what about November?
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but turns the interjection 'eh?' (meaning 'what?') round.
explanation.definitionFit: Then can mean next in order, as in 'first this, then that'.

clue.text: On record join Bread singer

indicators.note: on record means as heard on a recording, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to meet is to join, as where two lines meet
a loaf is a shaped mass of bread

explanation.surface: On a record, a band member joins the soft-rock group Bread as singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On record' turns MEET into MEAT by sound. Bread was a 1970s soft-rock band, but here it is just a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat Loaf was the American rock singer of Bat Out of Hell, so he is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Accept some money for watch

parts.note: to take something is to accept it
a banknote is a piece of money

explanation.surface: Someone accepts cash in exchange for a watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' looks like a timepiece but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To take note is to pay attention to something, so it means watch or observe.

clue.text: Oscar avoiding comparatively humourless artist

indicators.note: avoiding means the letter keeps out of the word, so it is dropped

parts.note: dourer is the comparative of dour, meaning stern and humourless
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An artist who shuns the Oscars and is rather grimmer than his peers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' takes one O out of DOURER. Albrecht Dürer was the German Renaissance painter and engraver.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a celebrated German painter and printmaker, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Safe from the flood — keeping daughter oblivious

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Noah's family were safe from the flood in the ark

explanation.surface: Noah's family survive the flood while one daughter stays unaware of it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts D inside IN THE ARK, the biblical refuge from the flood.
explanation.definitionFit: To be kept in the dark is an idiom for being uninformed, so it means unaware of what is going on.

clue.text: Sex? Nothing doing!

parts.note: love means nothing, zero, as in a tennis score
making and doing are both senses of carrying out or producing

explanation.surface: Someone asks about sex and is flatly refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing doing!' looks like a refusal; read literally it is LOVE (zero, as in tennis) plus MAKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovemaking is a gentle euphemism for sexual intercourse, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Vale! Leaving disheartened, having failed

indicators.note: having failed suggests something has gone wrong and broken apart, so the letters are rearranged
disheartened means the heart, the central letters, of leaving is taken out

explanation.surface: A farewell cry from someone leaving dejected after failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes AVI from the middle of LEAVING, leaving LENG; 'having failed' rearranges it. 'Vale!' looks like the Latin farewell, but here it means a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Vale and glen are both words for a valley, the glen typically narrow and Scottish.

clue.text: Like changes round pub — they work on the surface

indicators.note: round means placed about another piece, enclosing it

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
alters means changes
PH is the abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: Like changes made around the pub by workmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' makes the first two pieces go around the pub abbreviation, which lands at the join between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalters lay asphalt on roads and paths, so their work is literally on the surface.

clue.text: Wrong! Isn't that easy going round now

indicators.note: round means one part is placed around another, enclosing it
easy going suggests a loose, relaxed arrangement, so the letters are shuffled freely

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a task isn't that easy, demanding something happen right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'easy going' rearranges the first two words into THISTANT, and 'round' wraps that around the word for wrong. 'Wrong!' reads as an exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: This instant is an emphatic phrase for immediately, so it stands for now.

clue.text: Telling crook about books (probably stolen)

indicators.note: about means round, so the rearranged letters enclose the other piece
crook as an adjective means bent or out of shape, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A crook spinning a story about books that were probably nicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crook' looks like a criminal noun but is the Australian adjective for bent; it rearranges the first word into ILLGTEN, which 'about' wraps round the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-gotten means obtained by dishonest means, so applied to goods it suggests they were probably stolen.

clue.text: Leave home carrying penny metal fastener

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: to split is slang for leave
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone leaves home with a penny and a metal fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts the penny at the join between the two words; 'Leave' means the slang 'split', to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A split pin is a metal fastener with two prongs that are bent apart after insertion.

clue.text: Event in Illinois accounted for uprising

indicators.note: for uprising says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the following words, spanning them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An event in Illinois accounted for a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link, but it signals the letters sitting inside 'Illinois accounted'. In a Down clue 'uprising' reads upward, so NOISACCO turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion is a special happening or function, so it is a synonym of event.

clue.text: Meal that, for Spooner, needed something alcoholic

indicators.note: Spooner was known for swapping the initial sounds of words, so the opening letters change places

parts.note: lacked means needed or was without
punch is a mixed alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A meal that, in the Reverend Spooner's view, was missing a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: LACKED PUNCH with its initial letters swapped becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed lunch is food prepared at home and carried to eat later, so it is a kind of meal.

clue.text: Bundle of energy upset a lot of the same nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: do is short for ditto, the same

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in this Down clue the word is reversed

parts.note: many means a lot, a large number

explanation.surface: A lot of nurses who are all the same get upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses MANY to YNAM, which DO (ditto) 'nurses'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a lively, energetic person, used figuratively from the electrical generator.

clue.text: Suspend band on radio

indicators.note: on radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a frieze is a decorative horizontal band on a wall

explanation.surface: A band is taken off air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like musicians, but is a decorative strip, FRIEZE, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze something, such as pay or assets, is to suspend it at its current level.

clue.text: Vlad crosswords reportedly finish off country

parts.note: the setter Vlad refers to himself as I

indicators.note: finish off means the end of the phrase is cut away

parts.note: cross words spoken out are a rant, an angry tirade

explanation.surface: The setter Vlad's puzzles, so the gossip goes, see off a whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'crosswords' as cross words: Vlad's angry speech gives I RANT, and 'finish off' drops the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Royal 'leper' under pressure — he's not himself

indicators.note: under pressure suggests being squeezed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal outcast with leprosy, under strain, is no longer quite himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under pressure' rearranges ROYAL LEPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A role player takes on a character other than his own, so he is literally not being himself.

clue.text: News in Brussels on current malaise

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU
N is the abbreviation for new, so two of them give news
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: News coming out of Brussels about the current gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts NN, the abbreviation N for new written twice, inside EU, whose seat is Brussels; I (current) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a listless boredom and dissatisfaction, so it is a kind of malaise.

clue.text: Hard to stop virtuoso for long

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the letter fills the middle of the word

parts.note: an ace is an expert or virtuoso
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: It is hard to stop a virtuoso for long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stop' puts H inside ACE. 'long' looks like an adjective but is the verb, as in yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn for it, so it is a synonym of the verb long.

clue.text: Romeo in fix around college and university

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for fix

parts.note: to pin something is to fix it in place
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
C stands for circa, Latin for around
Eton College is the famous English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: Romeo is in a fix somewhere around a college and a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts Romeo inside the word for fix; 'around' is C, for circa; the college is Eton, the English public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton is an Ivy League university in New Jersey, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Cancel culture's ending? Heartless construct

indicators.note: ending says take only the final letter of the word
heartless means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to raise a building is to construct it

explanation.surface: A musing on cancel culture: is it ending, a cold and heartless construct?
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' gives E from culture's; 'Heartless' removes I from the middle of RAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or delete, so it is a synonym for cancel.

clue.text: Comedian's back, one with incisive material

indicators.note: back here means the rear, the final letter of the word

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
keen means sharp and incisive

explanation.surface: A comedian returns, a man with cutting material for his act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' takes the last letter, N, of Comedian's. 'material' looks like a comic's jokes but means cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanjing, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Coming on, tries to be inventive

indicators.note: inventive suggests creating something new from the pieces, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone making advances tries to be creative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inventive' rearranges ON TRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in store is about to happen or awaiting us, so it is coming.
